originalTitle: I hope Apple’s touchscreen MacBook takes some lessons from this Lenovo laptop

content: It looks like the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook might actually get announced next week, and after using the Lenovo Yoga 9n for our testing of Nvidia’s RTX Spark platform, it got me thinking: this is a lot of what I want from a touchscreen MacBook. Like the Apple silicon in modern MacBook Pros, RTX Spark is an Arm-based processor with a beefy integrated GPU and lots of unified memory. And the Yoga is the most fun RTX Spark laptop so far because it’s a 16-inch 2-in-1 convertible with a stylus. Its Nvidia-powered compatriots also have touchscreens, like most Windows laptops, but they’re conventional clamshell designs. The Lenovo Yoga does all your typical 2-in-1 stuff: it can be used as a clamshell laptop, and it can fold its hinge all the way back for tent mode and tablet modes. As a tablet, you can use it in either landscape or portrait orientation, and getting the keyboard out of the way is great for watching movies, playing games with a controller, or integrating your laptop into a multi-monitor desk setup with keyboard and mouse. [Image: 2-in-1s can be seen as a weird compromise between laptops and tablets. I just think they’re neat. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268814_Nvidia_RTX_Spark_HP_Lenovo_Yoga_9n_ADiBenedetto_0004.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Yoga 9n’s included stylus works for note-taking and drawing on its excellent OLED display, but you can also use it on the haptic trackpad for a Wacom-like experience, without blocking the screen with your hand. And the stylus is magnetic, allowing it to attach to the Yoga’s lid — either on its own, or while housed in its case. I particularly enjoy using the Yoga’s stylus for photo retouching in Lightroom Classic or Photoshop. I haven’t used a stylus for that kind of work in ages, since I gave up my old Wacom, but having one that works on either the screen or the trackpad is incredibly convenient I expect a touchscreen MacBook Pro would have Apple Pencil support. And like on the Lenovo, it would go a long way to get me back to using a stylus for retouching. But I hope that also like the Lenovo, it works on the trackpad too — the more options, the better. And if a touch-enabled MacBook supports the Apple Pencil (which it should), I’m also hoping it attaches to the laptop, both for convenience and for wireless charging, as on the iPad Pro. Lenovo’s stylus relies on USB-C charging, which is fine, but not as convenient as always having it charged and ready to go while attached to your laptop. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268814_Nvidia_RTX_Spark_HP_Lenovo_Yoga_9n_ADiBenedetto_0020.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268814_Nvidia_RTX_Spark_HP_Lenovo_Yoga_9n_ADiBenedetto_0016.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] I don’t expect Apple to make a standard convertible laptop after all this time. Simply joining Windows manufacturers in making a 2-in-1 or swapping the MacBook Pro’s Mini LED for a touchscreen OLED and calling it a day doesn’t seem very Apple. I’m hoping for something special, like Apple’s own take on the Microsoft Surface Laptop Studio — a clever idea that brought the touchscreen forward instead of flipping it backwards — or something totally fresh. And there are hints in macOS 27 that Apple is updating to Golden Gate to make touch functions feel more natural than just poking and prodding at things designed for a mouse cursor. As fun as I find 2-in-1 Windows laptops and Chromebooks, using those desktop operating systems with a finger or a stylus can get clunky. My hopes are high for Apple to wow us, because this MacBook Pro with touch is sure to be expensive. And Apple’s recent design decisions aren’t faultless. The HomeView’s lack of apps is perplexing. The iPhone Duo is a little messy. Current MacBooks are so great, it’s easy to forget the butterfly keyboard fiasco wasn’t all that long ago. After all this time of holding out on adding a touchscreen to the MacBook, Apple has to make it worth it. Photography by Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge

chineseContent: 看起来传闻已久的触摸屏 MacBook 可能会在下周正式发布，在使用联想 Yoga 9n 测试 Nvidia 的 RTX Spark 平台后，我开始思考：这就是我想要的触摸屏 MacBook 的很多功能。与现代 MacBook Pro 中的 Apple 芯片一样，RTX Spark 是一款基于 Arm 的处理器，具有强大的集成 GPU 和大量统一内存。 Yoga 是迄今为止最有趣的 RTX Spark 笔记本电脑，因为它是一款带有手写笔的 16 英寸二合一变形本。与大多数 Windows 笔记本电脑一样，其采用 Nvidia 技术的同类产品也配备了触摸屏，但它们是传统的翻盖式设计。联想 Yoga 具有所有典型的二合一功能：它可以用作翻盖式笔记本电脑，并且可以将其铰链完全向后折叠以实现帐篷模式和平板电脑模式。作为平板电脑，您可以横向或纵向使用它，并且将键盘移开非常适合观看电影、使用控制器玩游戏或将笔记本电脑集成到带有键盘和鼠标的多显示器桌面设置中。 [图片：二合一可以被视为笔记本电脑和平板电脑之间的一种奇怪的妥协。我只是觉得它们很整洁。 https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268814_Nvidia_RTX_Spark_HP_Lenovo_Yoga_9n_ADiBenedetto_0004.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Yoga 9n 附带的手写笔可在其出色的 OLED 显示屏上记笔记和绘图，但您也可以在触觉触控板可提供类似 Wacom 的体验，而不会用手挡住屏幕。触控笔具有磁性，可以单独固定在 Yoga 的盖子上，也可以放在盒子里。我特别喜欢使用 Yoga 的手写笔在 Lightroom Classic 或 Photoshop 中修饰照片。我已经很久没有使用手写笔来做这类工作了，罪过
